newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon sees TI deal anytime.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon sees TI deal anytime.

text.p: Raytheon Corp is in the final stages of its negotiations with the U.S. Justice Department on its proposed $3 billion takeover of Texas Instruments Inc's defense business and expects a decision anytime.
"We're in the final stages of discussions," Raytheon spokesman Robert McWade told Reuters. "Something could happen today. But that's still speculation on my part."

Sources close to the negotiations have said that the Justice Department is looking into how the merger would strengthen Raytheon's hand in strategic chip technology. Specifically, the Justice Department is examining Raytheon's strength in monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMICs) used in high-technology military applications such as aircraft radar and weapons systems, which makes up a very small part of the overall deal, the sources said.
"We're looking forward to completing this deal and moving forward to set our sites on closing the Hughes transaction later this year," McWade said.
Raytheon expects its proposed $9.5 billion takeover of Hughes Electronics Corp's defense business to close in the fall.
